text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Eleven people were killed in Punjab province in two bomb blasts and two shooting incidents.
- The Supreme Court of Pakistan asked state-run banks and financial institutions to submit details of written-off loans with names of beneficiaries and reasons for writing them off.
- State-run Karachi Electric Supply Corporation said it is losing 3.2 billion rupees a year to power theft, saying the main culprits are industrialists and residents of posh localities.
- Three key Pakistani nuclear establishments were put on an export ban list by the U.S. Commerce Department, it was officially announced in Washington.
- The Corporate Law Authority has proposed appointment of a quarter of directors of stock exchange boards from the private sector representing chartered accountants and investment banks.
- The government is actively considering a proposal to allow the Modarabas (Islamic mutual funds) to be converted into leasing companies and mutual funds.

- A World Bank loan for construction of the Ghazi Barotha Hydel Project will not be activated until the government settles claims of affectees of the Tarbela Dam amounting to over five billion rupees.

- A sum of 1.7 billion rupees received as donation in the Prime Minister's National Debt Retirement Programme has been used to retire the most expensive domestic debt carrying interest rate of 17.29 percent, the State (central) Bank of Pakistan said.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Total tax collection had reached 270 billion rupees by June 29, 16 billion rupees short of the revised target of 286 billion rupees for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June).
- Privatisation of the state-run Karachi Electric Supply Corporation will take place by December, KESC managing director Shahid Hamid said.

- A delegation of the International Monetary Fund is arriving in Islamabad on July 7 for two to three weeks of consultations with the authorities regarding the budget, the economic situation and the reforms planned by the government.
THE MUSLIM
- The government has decided to bring more than 400 serving army officers into law enforcing agencies to check the alarming deterioration in the law and order situation.
- The Supreme Court started hearing an application filed by an opposition senator regarding loans taken by the family of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif.
THE NATION
- The government has finalised a $700 million hydrocracker project with a UAE-based firm to manufacture white products from crude oil.
THE NEWS
- The Senate passed the 14th constitutional amendment bill, empowering party leaders to cancel the membership of any legislator for changing loyalties or violating party discipline.
- Police arrested around 200 activists of different sectarian parties in Lahore.
